subject: maths
question: If the marked price of an item is ₹1,500 and the selling price is ₹1,200, what is the percentage discount?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = 1500 − 1200 = 300

⇒ 1500 corresponds to 100%

⇒ 300 corresponds to (300 ÷ 1500) × 100

⇒ = 20%

**∴ Answer = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = 1500

Selling Price (SP) = 1200

**Formula:**

Discount% = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 1500 − 1200 = 300

⇒ Discount% = (300 ÷ 1500) × 100

⇒ = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ Percentage Discount = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Discount Formula:** Discount = MP − SP

**Successive Discount:** Net Discount = a + b − (ab ÷ 100)

**Marked Price Relation:** SP = MP − Discount

**Profit/Loss Link:** If SP > CP ⇒ Profit, if SP < CP ⇒ Loss
